findings.title: the parent's independent start-identity verification FAILS OPEN when the OS observation is unavailable, so a key-holding supervisor's forged process-start identity is accepted and the transfer reports an acknowledged supervisor
file_and_line: src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/activation-v4.mjs:19 — observedStartIdentity returns null on ANY /bin/ps failure
findings.mechanism: classifySupervisorClaim compares the claim's supervisor_start_identity against the parent's independent OS observation ONLY when that observation is non-null. observedStartIdentity returns null whenever /bin/ps throws or exits non-zero — proven dynamically here under genuine file-descriptor pressure (EMFILE, then EBADF), and equally reachable via EAGAIN/ENOMEM on the ps fork during a long multi-process run. When it is null the claim's self-reported start identity is never compared with anything, and the function returns ok:true. The claim is minted by the child, which legitimately holds the transferred ephemeral private key after reading the frame, so the child can sign ANY body it likes: every other binding (activation, payload, marker, intent, nonce, entrypoint digest, root object identity, PID) still passes, and the one field the child fully controls is the one that stops being checked. The asymmetry is decisive evidence this is an oversight rather than a design choice: the SUPERVISOR side of the identical observation fails CLOSED at lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:345 (`if (!observed) return R(LC_CODES.START_IDENTITY_MISMATCH)`). This is the defence that FG-CHK-197-02 was raised to protect (stale-PID / PID-reuse detection), and it silently disables itself under exactly the resource pressure a five-hour run creates.
reproduction: 1. Reachability, UNPATCHED: import src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/fixed-executables.mjs and activation-v4.mjs; fill the process fd table, release a fixed number, call fixedPs / observedStartIdentity. Observed: fixedPs THROWS (EMFILE at 4 free fds, EBADF across 5..30) and observedStartIdentity returns null.

2. Consequence, END TO END: build a disposable world (real git repo, real lifecycle root, disposable founder key, genuinely signed V4 activation), consumeActivationV4, createLaunchIntentV4 naming a supervisor entrypoint that reads fd 3, decodes the FGV4KEY1 frame, imports the ephemeral private key, and writes a fully valid ephemeral-signed claim whose supervisor_pid is its OWN pid and whose supervisor_start_identity is the literal string FORGED-START-IDENTITY-NEVER-OBSERVED. Run spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 with /bin/ps denied to the parent (node --import injects a throw for execFileSync('/bin/ps') in the parent only; /usr/bin/git verified still working; production source untouched; the child inherits neither the flag nor the injection because the boundary scrubs its env to PATH and HOME).
findings.observed_result: step 2 -> { ok: true, code: 'OK', supervisor_acknowledged: true, start_identity_independently_observed: false, supervisor_start_identity: 'FORGED-START-IDENTITY-NEVER-OBSERVED' }, claim accepted, claim_pid === spawned_pid === 951. step 3 (control) -> SUPERVISOR_CLAIM_INVALID, detail 'claim start identity FORGED-START-IDENTITY != OS-observed pid:86692|lstart:Sat Jul 25 12:00:03 2026'.
findings.required_result: when the parent cannot obtain an independent OS start identity the governed transfer must FAIL CLOSED with a structured SUPERVISOR_CLAIM_INVALID (or a dedicated START_IDENTITY_UNOBSERVABLE) refusal, matching the supervisor side at line 345. It must never accept the claim's self-reported identity, and it must never return ok:true with start_identity_independently_observed:false.
findings.aggravating_factor: tools/terminal0/lrcq/run-five-hour.mjs never reads start_identity_independently_observed (grep returns no occurrence), so the flag is reported but unenforced and nothing downstream can notice the skipped binding.
mitigating_factors: the ephemeral signature, PID equality and every digest binding still hold, so this is not a key escape and not an arbitrary-process acknowledgment: the forger must be the process this transfer actually spawned and must hold the transferred key
the fast-claim-and-exit race does NOT reach the branch (25/25 runs observed independently), so the exposure is resource-pressure-driven, not schedule-driven
no real activation exists today (active_keys is empty), so the defect is latent until enrollment
findings.narrow_correction_scope: one conditional in src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs. Make the start-identity comparison unconditional and treat a null observation as a refusal — e.g. replace line 538's guard with `if (observedStart === null) return bad('OS start identity unobservable'); if (d.supervisor_start_identity !== observedStart) return bad(...)`. Optionally re-observe once per poll iteration before deciding, so a single transient ps failure at t=0 does not condemn an otherwise healthy transfer. No other module, no schema change, no new caller option. Add one regression that denies the parent's OS observation and requires a non-OK code, plus one that requires start_identity_independently_observed to be true on every OK.

findings.mechanism: FN-F1-04 asserts that a 'validly shaped but wrong-PID / wrong-start-identity' claim is refused, and the contract lists 'wrong-start-identity' as an unconditional SUPERVISOR_CLAIM_INVALID outcome and describes the claim as bound to 'its OS-observed start identity'. Separately, the cited assertions FF1o-FF1q use a claim that is wrong in BOTH pid and start identity at once and is additionally unsigned, so it is refused at the signature check long before the start-identity comparison; FF1u observes start_identity_independently_observed === true in a single healthy run and cannot speak to the null case. The row therefore claims a control the evidence beneath it does not reach. This is the same class the lane has now produced three times (FG-FCHK-197-E, then FG-FFIN-197-F2 and F3): a row describing a mechanism the code does not unconditionally use.
